claim: Treat each thought as an action: compute only while expected gain in decision quality exceeds its cost. The myopic one-step version stops too early when no single step can change the choice; blinkered or multi-step lookahead fixes this.
agent_test: Compare a one-step 'would one more step change my answer' stop rule against a multi-step lookahead rule at equal token budget on tasks where early steps look useless.
caveat: The 1989 IJCAI precursor of Russell-Wefald was opened (d01): node savings but extra wall-clock time at depths 2-3, and the one-step rule failed against depth-6 alpha-beta. The 1991 journal paper itself was still not opened (403, d18). Hay 2012 is the formal source. No LLM test of one-step vs multi-step lookahead exists (gap 4 open).

claim: Optimal metalevel policies are expensive: metareasoning is itself an MDP, at least as hard as the base problem; so practical agents use cheap proxies (VOI, VPI, cost features) and metareasoning only pays when object-level compute is much costlier than the meta step.
agent_test: Count tokens spent on the gate itself; require gate cost below 10% of the saved thinking.

claim: A learned weighted mix of myopic VOI, VPI and cost approximates exact VOC very well in simulation (90.8-100% variance; 99.1% of optimal; 20.3% better than meta-greedy).
agent_test: Build a cheap proxy (answer-change probability times stakes minus token cost) and compare with fixed-depth thinking.
caveat: All four lines are one paper (Callaway 2018); simulation only.

claim: Humans plan roughly as VOC theory predicts but systematically stop early: 45% suboptimal computations still achieved 86.8% of max VOC; deviations 28.3% too early, 6.3% too late, 65.5% wrong node.
agent_test: Check whether the agent's own stopping errors skew early (too little) or late (too much); log both.
caveat: Lab toy tasks (Mouselab-MDP); one conference paper carries the deviation numbers.

claim: Reasoning models overthink easy problems: large token waste after the first correct answer, and savings from trimming are largest on easy sets.
agent_test: Cap thinking by difficulty tier; measure tokens saved and accuracy per tier.
caveat: Chen metrics are authors' own; mainly QwQ and R1 families.

claim: Length-penalty RL (RaM, Arora-Zanette, AdaptThink, Thinkless) cuts tokens 23-65% with accuracy kept or within about 5 points; the cost-in-the-reward form is VOC.
agent_test: Not testable by prompt alone; prompt analogue is a stated token budget plus a stop criterion.
caveat: All need training; math or closed-answer; no head-to-head between RaM and Arora.

claim: Trained length adaptation to difficulty is weaker than the headline: RaM's hard-vs-easy gap over STaR is clear for the 3B model (50.3 vs 34.4%) but absent for 8B (36.0 vs 35.9%); instruct models did not adapt (0.5-0.9%).
agent_test: Test whether our gate really shortens easy items more than hard ones, using a hard/easy split by direct-answer success.
caveat: One paper; easy label is a noisy proxy.

claim: Out of distribution, token savings transfer but accuracy does not always: RaM on MMLU-CF cut tokens 28-36%, but one model lost 3.8 points vs STaR.
agent_test: Evaluate any gate on a held-out domain, not only on tuning tasks.
caveat: Single paper, CIs about +-2.4.

claim: Chain-of-thought helps mostly on maths and symbolic tasks; elsewhere gains are near zero (110 papers: +14.2 symbolic, +12.3 math, +6.9 logic; other categories 56.8 vs 56.1). A gate should default to no chain for fact-recall tasks.
agent_test: Route fact-recall items to direct answer; compare accuracy and tokens vs always-CoT.
caveat: Meta-analysis of reported deltas; 95% of MMLU gain on '=' questions.

claim: Allocating test-time compute by prompt difficulty beats uniform best-of-N: about 4x less compute at equal accuracy on MATH (PaLM-2); easy items favour sequential revision, hard ones parallel search; little gain on the hardest.
agent_test: Bin items by a cheap difficulty probe; pick revise vs sample-more per bin at equal tokens.
caveat: One model family and benchmark; difficulty estimation costs compute; the 14x-pretraining claim depends on workload ratios.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Input-adaptive allocation from a learned difficulty predictor saves compute (code up to 50%, chat about 10%), but items with zero success probability waste budget.
agent_test: Add a give-up-or-escalate branch for items with no progress after k steps.
caveat: One paper; the two lines are the same source.

claim: Statistical stopping rules for self-consistency cut samples 3.3-7.9x (Adaptive-Consistency, accuracy drop 0.1-0.2% on average) and 34-80% (ESC), accuracy kept; they assume independent samples, which is false across models and probably worse within one.
agent_test: Implement a Beta or margin stop on repeated samples at equal tokens; check calibration under correlated samples (G4).
caveat: Same-model samples are correlated, so the stop can be overconfident. New: cross-model errors agree about 60% of the time vs 1/3 by chance (d12), and on hard queries more votes make accuracy fall (d13). Same-model calibration data is still absent. GPT-3.5 per-model drop was 0.2%, 4.4x fewer samples.

claim: More thinking can lower accuracy (negative value of computation): accuracy rises then falls with extended thinking, and inverse scaling appears on constructed tasks (R1 70% to 30%; Claude Opus 4 near 100% to 85-90%).
agent_test: Track accuracy against thought length per item; trigger stop when length passes a task-typical bound.
caveat: Constructed adversarial tasks; Ghosal's explanation rests on the authors' own model. Ordinary-benchmark case found: CoT below direct answering on easy GSM8K-Zero for Llama-3.1-8B (65.04 vs 70.32, d05) but not for GPT-4o-mini (99.50 vs 97.21). Puzzle 'collapse' is partly a token-limit artefact (d16). No base rate for real agent workloads (gap 9 open).

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without external feedback does not help and often hurts (GPT-3.5 CSQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 after 5 calls); a revise step has negative expected value unless a verifier exists.
agent_test: Allow revise only when an external check or tool result exists; compare to no-revise at equal tokens.
caveat: Single study, 2023 models; oracle labels restore gains.

claim: Underthinking is the opposite error: on hard problems models switch ideas too often; wrong answers have more switches and tokens. VOC must also stop abandoning promising lines.
agent_test: Count line switches per attempt; penalise switching before a line is checked.
caveat: Fix needs decoding access; only abstract numbers.

claim: Skipping or suppressing reflection can match thinking at much lower cost: NoThinking beats Thinking at small budgets (AMC23 51.3 vs 28.9 at 700 tokens); suppressing Wait/Hmm cuts length 27-51%; confidence early exit cuts 19-80%.
agent_test: At equal tokens compare direct answer, short plan, and full thinking; add confidence early exit.
caveat: Distilled R1 models; math; gap closes as budget grows; confidence can be overconfident. The c15 number was not re-verified. c15 re-checked (d17): 51.3 vs 28.9 at 700 tokens confirmed; it is budget-forced DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen only, and NoThinking lost 12-17 average points on Qwen3-4B/8B in d10.

claim: Agents should plan at an intermediate frequency: planning before every step and never planning both hurt; trained plan timing used 85% fewer tokens than a 70B model at similar reward.
agent_test: Compare plan-every-step, plan-never, and plan-on-trigger (stall or surprise) at equal tokens on a multi-step task.
caveat: Four environment/model settings (Crafter, POGS with Llama-3.3-70B; Gemini 2.5 Flash and TextWorld in the appendix) all show the intermediate-frequency peak (d06). Still no plan-on-surprise vs fixed-frequency test at equal tokens; Meta-Reasoner and SwiftSage are different benchmarks with self-reported gains.

claim: Model cascades save cost: cheap model first, escalate if a scorer is unsure (up to 98% cost cut at GPT-4 accuracy).
agent_test: Cheap pass first; escalate only when a verifier or agreement check fails.
caveat: Needs a trained scorer; selected datasets.

claim: Humans spend more time where deeper search is worth more: in 12M+ chess games move time rises with estimated benefit of search, more so for higher Elo, but the effect is modest and also present when true benefit is 0.
agent_test: Diagnostic only: correlate the agent's thinking length with an independent difficulty or benefit estimate.
caveat: Observational; Stockfish depth-1 proxy; Elo effect modest.

claim: A prompt-only budget or style change, no training, on closed-API models cuts output tokens 68-92% at near-equal accuracy on easy or symbolic maths items (GPT-4o-mini TALE-EP: GSM8K-Zero 99.50 to 98.72, 253 to 23 tokens; Chain of Draft: coin flip 100% kept, 68-86% fewer tokens), with a 4-8 point loss on harder items.
agent_test: Run a per-item budget estimate then a budget-capped answer on an easy and a hard set; report accuracy and total cost.
caveat: Maths and symbolic tasks only; CoD needs hand-written few-shot drafts and is weak zero-shot and on small models; accuracy loss grows with difficulty (-1 easy, -8 College).

claim: The gate has a cost: in TALE-EP the estimator call is counted, and savings fall from 91% fewer output tokens to 69% lower expense on easy items and to about 44% on the hardest set; accuracy at matched total tokens was not reported.
agent_test: Always report net cost including the difficulty-estimation call; compare to a flat cap at equal total tokens.
caveat: One paper, one model (GPT-4o-mini). Expense mixes input and cached tokens.

claim: Asking a model in plain words to 'plan only when necessary' does not work: it falls back to always or never planning, so adaptive timing needed SFT+RL. A hard-coded trigger (surprise, stall, error) is untested.
agent_test: Implement the trigger in code (not in the prompt) and compare with fixed k at equal tokens.
caveat: Authors' report of failed attempts, no numbers given; games only.

claim: No stop or switch signal is robustly best. Verbalised confidence is near chance for error prediction (GPT-4 AUROC 62.7%; GSM8K 54.8%), 5-sample agreement is much better (GSM8K 92.7%), logprob confidence and attention signals do about equally well on open models, and rankings flip between papers (DEER fine in one, worse on GSM8K and MATH-500 in another).
agent_test: Validate agreement, logprob or marker-triggered probes on our own tasks; do not use self-reported confidence as the stop signal.
caveat: Proposing groups run their own comparisons; open-weight models; no closed-API reasoning model was tested head to head.

claim: Errors are correlated across models: pairs of LLMs choose the same wrong answer about 60% of the time when both err (1/3 by chance), more so for more accurate models; plain majority voting can lose accuracy with more calls on hard queries. So agreement across samples is a floor on risk, not a probability.
agent_test: Check that the modal answer beats chance and add a difficulty guard before stopping on agreement.
caveat: Cross-model, multiple choice; same-model sample correlation not measured; d13 read abstract and introduction only.

claim: No cheap per-item rule predicts overthinking before the answer exists: on a 7B reasoning model difficulty explains little of non-convergence (r squared 0.186) and a hidden-state probe at token 150 reaches AUC 0.608; the practical signal is non-convergence under a token cap (43.5% of AIME generations, 11.5% accurate).
agent_test: Cap thinking per item and switch strategy at the cap; log non-convergence rate.
caveat: One small distilled model, maths, n = 200 for probes, preprint.

claim: The founding Russell-Wefald experiment (Othello, 1989) saved nodes (about 1/6 of depth-5 alpha-beta at slightly better than even) but used more wall-clock time at depths 2-3, and the one-step rule failed against depth-6 search. Savings needed per-depth tuning of the time-cost function.
agent_test: Treat the gate's own overhead as part of the budget and tune the cost weight per task type.
caveat: Only the 1989 IJCAI and UAI versions read; 1991 paper not opened; win counts unreadable; Othello only, authors' own test.
